The Secret List

FirefighterCloseCalls.com ↗ is an independent firefighter-safety newsletter. The site's founder has published it since 1998 with a focus on firefighter survival. Its sections include LODD reports, close-call submissions, behavioral health, and EMS close calls.

Research cross-reference

Rescue and mayday evidence

National survey findings paired with operational lessons from the 2026 incident set.

2026 Q1 aggregate

Firefighter Rescue Survey

  • 540 structure-fire incidents with rescues.
  • 1,033 civilians rescued—an average of 11.5 per day.
  • Only 10 of 1,033 rescues came from commercial structures.
  • Multifamily dwellings averaged 3.2 victims per incident.

Read the 2026 Q1 aggregate ↗

What this means for usThe survey reinforces the value of fast primary search and coordinated removal in residential occupancies, especially multifamily buildings.
Monthly snapshots · weekly distress reports · First 100

Firefighter Mayday Survey

Firefighter Mayday Survey ↗ and its Facebook page publish current incident snapshots and stat graphics for 10K followers. The “First 100” remains the latest full aggregate.

2026 monthly snapshots

  • July: 38 incidents—Tier 1: 1; Tier 2: 37. Connecticut led with 8 and New York with 5; leading factors included heat stress, electrical shock, collapse conditions, and multi-firefighter incidents.
  • June: 22 incidents—Tier 1: 1; Tier 2: 21. Reports included floor and ceiling falls, partial roof collapses, and an explosion injuring three firefighters.

Source: Firefighter Mayday Survey Facebook page, July 2026 snapshotJune snapshot: group-shared infographic; no direct post URL in the source data.

Weekly distress reports

  • May 18–25: 11 incidents involving partial collapses, trapped firefighters, disorientation, and a fatal fall across six cities.
  • September 2–12: 10 incidents involving collapse conditions, backdraft, burn injury, electrical shock, rescues, and hospitalizations.

Source: Firefighter Mayday Survey Facebook page, May 18–25, 2026 reportSource: Firefighter Mayday Survey Facebook page, September 2–12, 2026 report

First 100 refined stats

  • Emergency: floor fall 31.5%; lost/disoriented 23.6%; collapse 18.0%; cut off or overrun 10.1%.
  • Structure: homes 73.2%; low-rise apartments 9.8%; strip malls 7.3%; box stores 9.8%.
  • Emergency button: 86.4% did not activate it.
  • IC training: 57.7% lacked RIT/mayday-management training.
  • Who affected rescue: self-rescue 35.4%; own crew 28%; another interior company 17.1%; exterior company 11%; RIT 8.5%.
  • Egress: 65.8% were within 20 feet of the removal egress.

Source: Firefighter Mayday Survey Facebook page, First 100 stat graphicsRescue-path stat — First 100 report ↗Firefighter Mayday Survey ↗

What this means for usRehearse early mayday transmission, emergency-button use, decisive defensive transitions, and removal paths that exploit the distressed firefighter’s own crew and nearby companies.
12,851 departments · 2015–2021

Project Mayday

  • 30% of maydays occurred from 1–3 a.m.; 57% involved the first unit.
  • 52% occurred 20–35 minutes after arrival.
  • Survival path: self-rescue 36%, own crew 26%, another interior crew 25%.
  • RIT accounted for 7% of rescues.
  • One in nine RITs deployed for rescue had its own mayday.

Project Mayday analysis ↗

What this means for usBuild mayday prevention into first-unit discipline: complete the 360, track crews beyond the 20-minute mark, and practice crew-based rescue—not RIT reliance alone.

Scope and method

This is a curated operational review for , built from the linked reports. Dashboard rescues are structure-fire incidents only; drowning responses are excluded. Close calls are notable near-misses reported by FirefighterCloseCalls.com, not a complete national census. Florida incidents are prioritized. Mayday scanner items are explicitly marked unverified; USFA statuses remain provisional where applicable.
